title: Best Note-Taking Apps for Android in 2026: Obsidian vs Notion vs Google Keep vs UpNote
html:
We live in an era of information overload. Between research papers, meeting minutes, daily to-dos, code snippets, and random sparks of inspiration, capturing thoughts seamlessly on your smartphone is an essential superpower.

Last updated: 25 Nov 2026. This productivity guide compares the four leading note-taking systems on Android—Obsidian, Notion, Google Keep, and UpNote—evaluating offline reliability, Markdown portability, knowledge graph visualization, and subscription costs.

Yet choosing the wrong note app can be disastrous. If a service shuts down, changes its pricing tier, or locks your notes inside a proprietary database format, years of your intellectual work can be held hostage. Here is how the top Android note-taking tools compare and which one fits your workflow.

Direct Feature Comparison

Application Data Format Offline Performance Pricing Ideal Use Case
Obsidian Plaintext .md Markdown files 100% Offline (Local-First) 100% Free (Optional paid sync) Deep research, students, second brain
Notion Proprietary block cloud database Poor (Requires active internet) Free tier / Paid team plans Team project management & wikis
UpNote Rich text with Markdown support Fast offline sync Free tier / ₹2,499 Lifetime deal Clean, elegant Evernote alternative
Google Keep Proprietary sticky notes Instant sync 100% Free Quick grocery checklists & reminders

1. Obsidian: The Local-First "Second Brain" Revolution

If you want to own your notes forever, Obsidian is unmatched. Unlike cloud services where your text is stored in an encrypted company database, Obsidian stores every single note as a plain .md (Markdown) text file in a folder on your phone's internal storage.

Even if Obsidian as a company disappeared tomorrow, your notes remain completely accessible in any text editor on Windows, Mac, Linux, or Android. Obsidian's superpowers include:

  • Bidirectional Linking: Type [[Topic]] to interconnect concepts across different subjects, building a personal Wikipedia of your knowledge.
  • Interactive Graph View: Visually renders relationships between ideas as an animated cosmic web of interconnected nodes.
  • Community Plugin Ecosystem: Thousands of community plugins let you add Kanban boards, Excalidraw whiteboards, spaced-repetition flashcards, and calendar journaling.

2. Notion: The Collaborative Database Giant

Notion is not just a note app; it is a full-fledged relational database platform. If you want to organize a college semester with customized course schedules, embed reading lists with status tags, or manage a startup sprint board, Notion's aesthetic templates and drag-and-drop flexibility are extraordinary.

The Catch: Notion is built for desktop web browsers first. On Android, the app acts essentially as a webview wrapper. It takes 2 to 3 seconds to cold boot and struggles significantly when you have poor cellular coverage on trains or in basements.

3. UpNote: The Under-the-Radar Polish Champion

Remember when Evernote was the king of notes before it became bloated, slow, and expensive? UpNote is what modern Evernote should have been.

Available across Android, Windows, Mac, and iOS, UpNote opens instantly, formats code blocks and tables beautifully, supports nested notebooks, and features one of the few remaining affordable lifetime purchase licenses in tech. For users who want a polished, distraction-free writing environment without managing Markdown files, UpNote is a joy to use.

4. Google Keep: The Instant Scratchpad

Google Keep should not be used for writing a thesis or organizing long-form documentation. But for grocery lists, photo receipts, quick voice memos that transcribe audio to text in real-time, and color-coded sticky reminders, Keep is unbeatable because of its speed.

The Final Verdict: Which One Should You Download?

  1. Choose Obsidian if: You are a student, programmer, researcher, or writer who wants total data ownership, offline reliability, and interconnected knowledge graphs.
  2. Choose Notion if: You need collaborative databases, client portals, and aesthetic project management tables.
  3. Choose UpNote if: You want a clean, elegant notebook app that syncs seamlessly across phone and PC without complex configuration.
  4. Keep Google Keep installed: As your fast 2-second capture inbox on your home screen.

faq.title: Is Obsidian completely free on Android?
faq.description: Yes. Obsidian's core app and full plugin ecosystem are completely free for personal use. You only pay if you choose to use their proprietary end-to-end encrypted cloud sync service.

faq.title: Can I sync Obsidian notes for free between Android and PC?
faq.description: Yes. You can sync your Obsidian folder using free tools like Syncthing, Git, or Google Drive / Remotely Save plugins without paying for Obsidian Sync.

faq.title: Why does Notion feel slow on Android phones?
faq.description: Notion is an electron-based web application that fetches data from remote cloud databases. Unlike local-first apps like Obsidian, Notion must ping servers before rendering complex pages.
